claim: On v3 detecting-insults, opus on designer alone (with sonnet on all other 8 roles) DOES NOT fix the schema gate. Pipeline ran to completion at $7.01 with valid_submission=False (missing Comment column). Designer alone is not the schema bridge — neither at the sonnet level (X217) nor at the opus level (X231). The schema gate on detecting requires opus on more than designer or on a different role entirely.

support.grader_error: Submission should have an Comment column

scope: Single Phase 2 run. Adds to the 7-negative-streak on detecting.

consolidated_findings_on_detecting.what_we_know_now: Schema gate on detecting v3 is NOT crossable by: any haiku variant, any single sonnet lift, any sonnet-everywhere, any opus-designer-alone. Phase 1 opus-everywhere ($342) is the only known crossing.
consolidated_findings_on_detecting.remaining_single_opus_hypotheses: opus-aggregator (X232 queued), opus-coder (un-queued; would be $5-10 in non-coder roles + opus-coder probably $200+)
consolidated_findings_on_detecting.remaining_pair_opus_hypotheses: opus on {designer + aggregator} (X233 queued), {designer + coder}, {coder + aggregator}
consolidated_findings_on_detecting.pessimistic_outlook: If even opus-on-2-roles fails, the schema gate is multi-role opus, and savings on detecting are extremely limited. The bandit may need to escalate to triple-opus.

limitations: n=1 per probe; very expensive to escalate further (each detecting cycle is now $7-10).

follow_up_experiments: X232 (queued, high priority) — opus-aggregator alone probe
X233 (queued, medium priority) — opus on both designer + aggregator (if X232 also fails this is the next step up)
implications.consider_giving_up_on_detecting: After X232 and X233, if all opus-on-N-roles probes fail (N=1,2), the practical recommendation may be: 'detecting requires opus on all 9 roles; cost is $342 fixed; do not attempt cost-savings on this task family.'
